summary: Build an app for a peer-to-peer rental marketplace focused on renting out unused garage tools.

existing_features.title: Implement Internet Identity sign-in and a basic user profile flow. Store a minimal profile (display name and optional contact note) tied to the authenticated principal, and expose create/read/update endpoints for the signed-in user.

Build the tool listing feature: allow an authenticated owner to add, edit, and remove garage tool listings with fields: title, category, description, condition, daily price, optional security deposit, location (city/area text), availability flag, and photos. Photos must be managed on the frontend; store only image references/URLs/asset paths in the backend.

Implement marketplace browsing for tool listings with search and filters: keyword search over title/description, category filter, price range filter, and an 'available only' toggle. Provide sorting options (newest, price low-to-high, price high-to-low) and a responsive listings grid.

Add a rental request and booking workflow: renters can request a date range for a tool; owners can approve or decline; approved requests become bookings and block availability for that tool for the approved date range. Support at least the statuses: Requested, Approved, Declined, Cancelled, Completed.

Create user dashboards: 'My Tools' (owner listings and their statuses), 'Requests' (incoming requests for owners), and 'My Rentals' (requests/bookings for renters). Each item must link to the corresponding tool and rental detail views.

Apply a coherent visual theme suitable for a garage/tool marketplace across the app (colors, typography, spacing, and component styling), avoiding a blue/purple primary palette. Use the existing UI component library by composing components rather than editing immutable UI sources. Add generated static brand imagery (logo and hero/landing illustration) under frontend/public/assets/generated and reference them directly from the frontend.

new_feature_requests.summary: Create a peer-to-peer garage tool rental app (list tools, browse/search, and rent between individuals).

Implement Internet Identity sign-in and a basic user profile flow so users can act as tool owners and renters. Store a minimal profile (display name and optional contact note) associated with the authenticated principal.

Create a tool listing feature where an owner can add, edit, and remove garage tool listings with key details: title, category, description, condition, daily price, security deposit (optional), location (city/area text), availability flag, and photos (frontend-managed; store image references/URLs/asset paths in backend).

Implement marketplace browsing with search and filters for tool listings, including: keyword search (title/description), category filter, price range filter, and an 'available only' toggle. Provide a responsive listings grid with sorting (e.g., newest, price low-to-high, price high-to-low).

Add a rental request and booking workflow: renters can request a date range for a tool; owners can approve or decline; approved requests become bookings and block availability for that tool for the approved date range. Track rental status transitions at minimum: Requested, Approved, Declined, Cancelled, Completed.

Create user dashboards: 'My Tools' (owner listings and their statuses), 'Requests' (incoming requests for owners), and 'My Rentals' (requests/bookings for renters). Each item should link to the corresponding tool and rental detail views.

Define and enforce core backend data models and access control in the single Motoko actor for: UserProfile, ToolListing, RentalRequest/Booking, and basic query endpoints for browsing (with search/filter parameters) and per-user dashboards. Ensure stable persistence across upgrades for these records.

Apply a coherent visual theme across the app (colors, typography, spacing, and component styling) suitable for a garage/tool marketplace, avoiding a blue/purple primary palette. Use the existing UI component library by composing components rather than editing immutable UI sources.

Add generated static brand imagery to the frontend and use it in the UI: include a logo and a hero/landing illustration, stored under frontend/public/assets/generated, and referenced directly by the frontend (not served through the backend).

Create backend data models and access control in the single Motoko actor for: UserProfile, ToolListing, and RentalRequest/Booking (including rental status transitions Requested, Approved, Declined, Cancelled, Completed). Ensure only owners can modify their listings and only involved parties can view/manage their requests/bookings.

Implement stable persistence across upgrades for all core records (profiles, listings, rental requests/bookings) in the backend, preserving existing data during canister upgrades under the single-actor architecture.
